clue.text: About to follow Jude, upset by Law

indicators.note: to follow tells us the piece for about comes after the rearranged name
upset means the four letters of the name Jude are knocked into a new order

parts.note: re is a short word for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone named Jude is upset by the law, with something about to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law' looks like part of the surface's legal setting, but 'by Law' is the definition, a Latin phrase meaning by right of law.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means according to the rule of law, as opposed to in practice.

clue.text: Heart of Nazareth erected for building firm

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here the middle two of Nazareth

parts.note: something erected is put up, so this gives up

explanation.surface: The centre of Nazareth has been built up by a construction company.
explanation.walkthrough: Nazareth has eight letters, so its heart is the fourth and fifth, AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arup is a well-known international engineering and design consultancy behind many major buildings.

clue.text: Redesign of note in measuring a few yards

indicators.note: redesign means the letters of the three words are rebuilt in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A redesign of something noteworthy is set out over a few yards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redesign' shuffles OFNOTEIN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine feet make exactly three yards, so something of that length measures a few yards.

clue.text: Tosses about soup utensils, leaving area unprotected

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: shies means throws or tosses

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for area departs from the utensils

parts.note: ladles are the deep spoons used to serve soup

explanation.surface: Someone flings soup ladles around and leaves a whole area exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tosses' looks like the definition's partner, but it is a synonym for throwing, not a verb acting on the utensils.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter without a shield has no cover against blows, hence unprotected.

clue.text: Isolated spot played up endlessly

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards
endlessly means the final letter of the word for played is dropped

parts.note: toyed means played, as with a toy

explanation.surface: A remote place was played up, though never quite to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TOYED to TOYE, and 'up' turns that round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small island in a river, a spot cut off by water.

clue.text: Sailor put down for wide-ranging craft

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
dis is slang for disrespect or put down

explanation.surface: A seaman is humiliated for the sake of an ambitious vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the time-and-space machine in the long-running British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor's time machine roams across all of space and history, a vehicle of unlimited range.

clue.text: China's difficult question over corruption

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzling or tricky question
vice is moral corruption or depravity

explanation.surface: A tricky question about corruption in the Chinese state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is the porcelain; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cups, saucers and teapot is commonly made of porcelain, known as china.

clue.text: Perhaps worming out of teaching when the heart's not in it

indicators.text: when the heart's not in it
indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, which is removed here

parts.note: education is teaching or instruction

explanation.surface: Getting information out of someone, in a teaching style, without real enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: EDUCATION has nine letters, so its heart is the fifth, A; removing it leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eduction is the act of drawing out or extracting, of which extracting worms is one example.

clue.text: Nobel ultimately received by what productive German bacteriologist?

parts.note: eh is a questioning exclamation like what

indicators.note: received by means the letter goes into the following word

parts.note: rich means fertile or productive, as of soil

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Nobel

explanation.surface: A question about which productive German germ scientist finally won the Nobel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives L, which 'received by' puts into RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Ehrlich was the German pioneer of chemotherapy who won the 1908 Nobel Prize in medicine.

clue.text: Accountant's deadline wanted to have switch-over just before completion

indicators.text: to have switch-over just before completion
indicators.note: two letters near the end of the word swap places, a switch-over just short of the finish

parts.note: yearned means longed for or wanted

explanation.surface: An accountant wanted the system switched over just before the work was finished.
explanation.walkthrough: In YEARNED the N and E just before the final D change places, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of the financial year is when the books must be finalised, a key date in accounting.

clue.text: One priest and equable Father in sitcom like a Catholic birth

parts.note: un is a dialect form of one, as in a good un
even means calm or equable
Father Ted is the title priest of the Irish sitcom Father Ted

explanation.surface: A priest and a calm cleric from a TV comedy discuss a Catholic birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is a 1990s sitcom about Irish priests. The definition is a joke: the Church forbids contraception, so births are not prevented.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic teaching rules out contraception, so a birth in that tradition is not stopped beforehand.

clue.text: Part of kangaroo's a capacious pouch

indicators.note: part of means the letters are a stretch found within the following words

explanation.surface: A kangaroo has a roomy pouch as part of its body.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac is a bag-like cavity in an animal or plant, a natural pouch.

clue.text: Say doctor that hurts German's the wartime substitute for baker

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say
GP stands for general practitioner, a family doctor
ow is the cry of someone in pain
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone tells a doctor that the German version hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: Dried egg was the rationed British cook's stand-in for fresh eggs in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried, powdered egg replaced fresh eggs in home baking during rationing in the Second World War.

clue.text: Organised drug run in Georgia: those doing it keep singing

indicators.note: in means the run of pieces sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
ran means organised or managed, as in ran a company
dope is slang for a drug
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A drug-running operation in Georgia is set up by people who won't stop singing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: in this style of opera every line is sung, with no spoken dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of opera is sung throughout, so its performers never break into ordinary speech.

clue.text: Cylinder part with missing top getting returned again

parts.note: a reel is a cylinder on which thread or film is wound

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which goes missing here

parts.note: section means part

explanation.surface: A spool has lost its top section and is being sent back once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with missing top' takes S from SECTION, leaving ECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning a second consecutive vote means being sent back to office by the voters once more.

clue.text: Retiring, live in island hotel surrounded by sand?

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
in means one word sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: are means exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone retiring goes to live in a desert island hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'Retiring', turns the whole container round, so the island abbreviation ends up at both edges of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai, or caravanserai, is an inn for travellers across desert country.

clue.text: Old log-book format?

parts.note: an old log was once a tree that has died, and a book format is a printing; together they describe a newspaper on paper rather than online

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the printed version of a newspaper or book, made from pulped timber rather than shown on screen.

clue.text: Broadcast cop duo as reality TV

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A pair of police officers appear on air as a reality show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges COPDUOAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A docusoap is a fly-on-the-wall documentary series following real people, a type of reality television.

clue.text: Nude frolicking in semi-ingenuous double entendre?

indicators.note: in means the shuffled word goes inside the other piece
semi means half, so only the first half of the word for ingenuous is used

parts.note: innocent means naive or ingenuous

indicators.note: frolicking suggests playing about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A naked romp in a half-innocent risque joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-' halves a synonym, not the printed word: take the first four letters of an eight-letter word for ingenuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Innuendo is suggestive hinting, the stock in trade of a risque double meaning.

clue.text: Roughly billions wiped from liability for military trainee

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly

indicators.note: wiped from means the letter for billions is erased from the word that follows

parts.note: a debt is a liability

explanation.surface: Roughly a billion has been written off a liability for an army trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiped from' removes B from DEBT to leave DET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Hooch minder who works in rotation

definitions.meaning: in the film ... and Hooch, a detective looks after a slobbering dog called Hooch
someone who shapes wood or metal on a spinning lathe

explanation.definitionFit: Tom Hanks's detective minds the dog Hooch in the film, and a lathe operator shapes things as they spin.

clue.text: Tie's frayed where it's worn, constricting black US writer

indicators.note: frayed means the letters of the word are worn into a different order

parts.note: tie's stands for tie is, giving the four letters

indicators.note: constricting means one piece is squeezed inside the other

parts.note: a tie is worn round the neck
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A frayed tie squeezes the neck of a black American author.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of "Tie's" stands for 'is', so it supplies a letter; the black piece goes into the word for where a tie is worn.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck was the American novelist of The Grapes of Wrath.

clue.text: Was wailing in haunt a frightful cry from below?

indicators.note: in a down clue from below means reading upwards, so the pieces are backwards

parts.note: a den is a favourite haunt or hideout
eek is a squeal of fright

explanation.surface: In a haunted place a terrified scream rises from underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from below' turns DENEEK round.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to lament the dead with a high wail, so keened is wailed in grief.

clue.text: Rudiments of sophistication in people showing little taste

indicators.note: rudiments are the very beginnings, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: People who show little taste lack even the basics of sophistication.
explanation.definitionFit: A sip is a small mouthful of drink, just a taste.

clue.text: Bankside playhouse was erected in that location, present for entering

parts.note: rose means went up or was erected

indicators.note: for entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: there means in that place
at means present, as in at the meeting

explanation.surface: A theatre was built in that spot by the Thames, a gift for those who come in.
explanation.walkthrough: Bankside is the south bank of the Thames in London, home of the Elizabethan Rose and Globe theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rose was an Elizabethan playhouse on the south bank of the Thames, built in 1587.

clue.text: To hell with a diluter of spirits! …

parts.note: sod, as in sod it, is a British oath meaning to hell with

explanation.surface: A drinker damns the mixer added to whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sod' is a mild British curse, used as 'sod it' or 'sod that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water is often added to whisky or brandy to dilute it.

clue.text: … This girl's almost finished another one

indicators.note: almost finished means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: following the previous clue, another diluter of spirits is tonic, mixed with gin

explanation.surface: A girl has nearly finished another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue: 'another one' means another diluter of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Toni is a girl's name, a short form of Antonia.

clue.text: Booby is to help catching flightless bird

indicators.note: catching means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: aid means to help
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A booby bird helps to trap a flightless bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booby' looks like the seabird, matching the bird theme; it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby is a stupid person, the same as a scatterbrained fool.

clue.text: I'm taking orders to eat, dividing product of mine

indicators.note: dividing means the word splits the other in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: ore is the raw material produced by a mine
dine means to eat

explanation.surface: A waiter takes orders for dinner, splitting the output of a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' looks like a restaurant's; it means holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A person being ordained into the clergy is entering holy orders, admitted to the ministry.
